Both anchors are long-term orthopedic follow-up cohorts of treated patients, so individual claims require the date and age at diagnosis with the Stulberg class where documented, the treatment history (non-operative containment, varus derotational osteotomy, pelvic osteotomy, or arthroplasty), dated radiographs with a validated hip osteoarthritis grade, and exclusion of the competing causes listed on the edge.

Family, constitutive-identity, and duplicate-scope guards: no legg-calve-perthes-disease -> avascular-necrosis edge is authored because the disease IS idiopathic osteonecrosis of the femoral head and the generic avascular-necrosis identity is the umbrella, following the kienbock-s-disease and freiberg-s-infraction pattern; the target is the generic osteoarthritis identity rather than post-traumatic-osteoarthritis because the condition is non-traumatic and the post-traumatic identity is reserved for injury-driven pathways; no -> muscle-atrophy edge (zero-record for condition-specific quantification, and the located limb-length and abductor findings are surgical-series measurements rather than a catalog diagnosis), no -> unexplained-chronic-pain edge (the pain in the located cohorts is lesion-explained and that identity is reserved for unexplained presentations), and no -> loss-of-use-of-extremities or -> joint-replacement-residuals edge (rating-framework and post-surgical-container guards; arthroplasty is a treatment step, not a secondary condition).
governanceNotes: D1 batch 52 (2026-09-24): one bounded association edge authored - legg-calve-perthes-disease to osteoarthritis (rank 1) - classified ASSOCIATION_ONLY with etiologicalConsensus NOT_ESTABLISHED, vaNexusProbabilityAlignment NOT_ASSERTED, and hypothesizedOnly:true; mechanismCategory BIOMECHANICAL_ALTERATION. The proposition rests on the Onishi 2011 retrospective analysis of 67 patients (70 hips) treated for Perthes' disease at a mean follow-up of 36.1 years and a mean age of 43.1 years, in which only 48% of hips in the radiographically evaluated group had no osteoarthritis (Tonnis grade 0), good radiographic results (Stulberg class I or II) were achieved in 59% of hips, the Tonnis grade and JOA score declined after 40 years of age with all patients older than 50 years showing severe osteoarthritis and osteoarthritis severity correlating significantly with age at follow-up, and younger age at diagnosis (under 8 years) correlated with a better result (PMID 21258809), and on the Shohat 2016 long-term follow-up of 40 patients (43 hips) treated with varus derotational osteotomy at a mean 42.5 years (range 32.4-56.5) and mean age 50.2 years, in which 7 patients (7 hips; 17% of the 41 hips with information available) underwent total hip arthroplasty for hip pain, 16 of 28 hips with radiographs (57.1%) had no or minimal signs of osteoarthritis, the Stulberg classification was associated with the Harris hip score, the SF-36 score, hip pain, a Trendelenburg sign, coxa magna, and the Tonnis grade, and it was the only factor associated with fair or poor outcomes on multivariate analysis (PMID 27489318). Deformity of the femoral head and acetabulum after the childhood ischemic episode therefore co-occurs with, and is graded in, hip osteoarthritis decades later.

Counter-evidence and caveat screens recorded 2026-09-24: (i) treatment-mediated ascertainment - both cohorts are treated surgical series (varus derotational osteotomy, triple pelvic osteotomy, or arthroplasty candidates), so the natural history of unoperated disease is not described and the surgery itself alters joint mechanics; (ii) age-dependent expression and ceiling effects - the Onishi cohort reported no total hip arthroplasty in either group while all patients older than 50 years showed severe osteoarthritis, so the outcome is strongly age-driven and the cohorts' endpoints and questionnaires differ (JOA plus radiographs in one group, postal questionnaires in the other); (iii) classification dependence - the Stulberg classification is a sphericity and congruity grade rather than a severity-of-arthritis measure, and it was the dominant predictor of outcome, so the individual course depends on the residual deformity rather than on the diagnosis alone; (iv) competing causes - developmental dysplasia of the hip, slipped capital femoral epiphysis, previous trauma or infection, femoroacetabular impingement, inflammatory arthritis, and age-related primary osteoarthritis independently produce the same radiographic patterns, and the juvenile-arthroplasty literature groups Perthes' disease among these causes (PMID 33066797).

Negative screens recorded 2026-09-24: (i) no legg-calve-perthes-disease-to-avascular-necrosis edge - the disease is itself femoral-head osteonecrosis, so the generic identity is the umbrella (constitutive-identity guard, the kienbock-s-disease precedent); (ii) no edge to post-traumatic-osteoarthritis - that identity is reserved for injury-driven pathways while Perthes' disease is non-traumatic (wrong-target guard); (iii) no -> muscle-atrophy edge - the located cohorts report Harris hip and JOA function, Stulberg class, coxa magna, Trendelenburg sign, and limb-length restoration after arthroplasty rather than quantified muscle atrophy (zero-record guard); (iv) no -> unexplained-chronic-pain edge - the pain in these cohorts is attributed to the degenerate joint, and that identity is reserved for unexplained presentations (wrong-target guard); (v) no -> joint-replacement-residuals or -> loss-of-use-of-extremities edge (post-surgical-container and rating-framework guards); (vi) no -> scoliosis or limb-length-discrepancy edge (no leg-length-discrepancy identity exists and the located limb-length data are arthroplasty-series measurements rather than a diagnosed secondary condition).

nexusClaim.associationBasis: The Onishi 2011 retrospective analysis of 67 patients (70 hips) treated for Perthes' disease at a mean follow-up of 36.1 years (mean age 43.1 years) found that only 48% of hips in the radiographically evaluated group had no osteoarthritis (Tonnis grade 0), that the Tonnis grade and JOA score declined after 40 years of age with all patients older than 50 years showing severe osteoarthritis and osteoarthritis severity correlating significantly with age at follow-up, and that younger age at diagnosis (under 8 years) correlated with a better result; the Shohat 2016 long-term follow-up of 40 patients (43 hips) after varus derotational osteotomy at a mean 42.5 years reported total hip arthroplasty in 7 patients (17% of the 41 hips with information available), no or minimal osteoarthritis signs in 16 of 28 hips with radiographs (57.1%), an association of the Stulberg classification with Harris hip score, SF-36, hip pain, Trendelenburg sign, coxa magna, and Tonnis grade, and the Stulberg classification as the only factor associated with fair or poor outcomes on multivariate analysis; the literature documents graded hip osteoarthritis decades after Perthes' disease without establishing that the childhood disease caused an individual's arthritis.
nexusClaim.causationStatus: The mapping does not assert that Perthes' disease caused an individual's hip osteoarthritis: both cohorts are treated surgical series without an untreated natural-history comparison, osteoarthritis expression in the located data is strongly age-dependent (all patients older than 50 years showed severe osteoarthritis in one cohort while the other reported no arthroplasty), the dominant predictor was the residual Stulberg deformity rather than the diagnosis itself, and developmental dysplasia, slipped capital femoral epiphysis, prior trauma or infection, femoroacetabular impingement, inflammatory arthritis, and age-related primary osteoarthritis independently produce the same radiographic pattern - so no directional or probability claim is made.

causalMechanism.primaryVector: A hypothesized deform-arthrosis route is described: the childhood ischemic episode leaves the femoral head flattened and the acetabulum dysplastic, so the articulating surfaces are incongruent and the hip is placed under abnormal contact stress, which produces progressive cartilage loss and secondary osteoarthritis decades later; the located cohorts document that residual deformity (Stulberg classification, coxa magna, Tonnis grade) tracks the long-term functional outcome, which supports the mechanism but does not establish the individual causal share of the childhood disease relative to coexisting structural and age-related factors.

evidentiaryProfile.conservativeRationale: This relationship is supported as an association only. Long-term follow-up cohorts of treated Perthes' disease document hip osteoarthritis and arthroplasty in a substantial minority to majority of patients, but individual determination requires the age and date at diagnosis with Stulberg grading where documented, treatment history, dated radiographs with a validated osteoarthritis grade, and exclusion of the competing structural and inflammatory hip causes, with review by a qualified medical professional.
evidentiaryProfile.evidenceGaps: Orthopedic documentation of Legg-Calve-Perthes disease with the age and date at diagnosis, laterality, radiologic stage or Stulberg classification at skeletal maturity, and any treatment (non-operative containment, varus derotational osteotomy, pelvic or femoral osteotomy) with dates; dated hip radiographs with a validated osteoarthritis grade (for example Tonnis) and serial comparison showing progression, plus the residual deformity findings (coxa magna, femoral-head sphericity, acetabular dysplasia, limb-length difference); functional documentation (Harris hip score, JOA score, range of motion, Trendelenburg sign, gait, and pain pattern) with dates; documentation of any total hip arthroplasty or other reconstructive surgery and its indication; exclusion of developmental dysplasia of the hip, slipped capital femoral epiphysis, prior hip trauma, septic or tuberculous arthritis, femoroacetabular impingement, inflammatory arthropathy, osteonecrosis from another cause (corticosteroid, alcohol, sickle cell, or diving-related), and age-related primary osteoarthritis; orthopedic assessment of whether the documented Perthes' disease materially contributed to the osteoarthritis
alternativeEtiologiesToRuleOut: Slipped capital femoral epiphysis or prior ipsilateral hip trauma
Femoroacetabular impingement or other structural impingement
Sequelae of septic or tuberculous arthritis or of other hip infection
Corticosteroid-, alcohol-, sickle-cell-, or decompression-related osteonecrosis with secondary collapse
Inflammatory arthropathy (rheumatoid arthritis, spondyloarthropathy, or crystal arthropathy)
Age-related primary hip osteoarthritis or a generalized osteoarthritis phenotype

suggestions.rationale: Authored at ASSOCIATION_ONLY following the freiberg-s-infraction, kienbock-s-disease, and avascular-necrosis osteoarthritis family: two long-term follow-up cohorts (36.1 and 42.5 years) document that a substantial proportion of treated hips develop osteoarthritis, one with a clear age-dependency and both with the residual deformity grade as the dominant predictor. Because the cohorts are surgically treated series without untreated comparisons, the outcome is strongly age-linked, and several structural and inflammatory hip causes produce the same pattern, the conservative standard keeps the edge at association only and does not author the constitutive avascular-necrosis twin or the post-traumatic-osteoarthritis variant.
